issues.description: Storing a live FrameProcessor reference on a control frame is the wrong shape
issues.detail: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame.service holds a full FrameProcessor handle rather than a stable identifier. Control frames should carry value-like identity (name/id), not live runtime objects. This couples the frame to mutable processor state, breaks serialization, retains swapped-out services via GC, and invites identity-vs-equality bugs. Pass a service name or id and resolve at the switcher.

issues.description: Suppression check relies on default == identity comparison without stating the invariant
issues.detail: `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` falls back to object identity on FrameProcessor. If a subclass overrides __eq__, or the active service is wrapped/proxied/re-instantiated, the switcher silently fails open and the internal control frame leaks downstream. Use `is`, or compare a stable id, and document the invariant explicitly.

issues.description: Consumption contract for the request frame is unstated and split across components
issues.detail: Previously the switcher consumed RequestMetadataFrame unconditionally; now STTService re-pushes it and the switcher suppresses only when service matches active. The postcondition (frame invisible downstream) silently weakens outside a switcher or for subclasses that override process_frame. Document the handler contract on the frame and STTService, or centralize the re-push so subtypes cannot forget.

issues.description: Forward-reference annotation "FrameProcessor" is unresolved and unimported in frames.py
issues.detail: The dataclass field annotation is a string, so construction works, but FrameProcessor is not imported in this module. Any get_type_hints call, pydantic adapter, or schema introspection will fail to resolve it. Either add a TYPE_CHECKING import or weaken the annotation to Any with a docstring contract.

issues.description: Rename is a breaking public-API change with no deprecation alias
issues.detail: RequestMetadataFrame was an exported symbol; renaming it outright breaks downstream importers on the next version bump. A one-line `RequestMetadataFrame = ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame` alias with a DeprecationWarning costs nothing and preserves backward compatibility. A changelog entry alone is insufficient.

issues.description: Switcher-internal frame lives in the global frames module without a literate suppression comment
issues.detail: The frame is explicitly switcher-internal yet sits alongside public frames in pipecat.frames.frames, blurring the module boundary. The push_frame suppression branch also lacks a one-line comment stating the invariant ("request frame arrives here only after the targeted active service handled it"), making the logic hard to audit.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the rename and targeting refinement are structurally sound but flags one dominant taste/design issue: the new control frame embeds a live FrameProcessor reference and relies on default == identity to drive switcher suppression. All three reviewers want a stable identifier instead of a processor handle, and an explicit invariant for the equality check. Secondary concerns cluster around an unstated consumption contract now split between STTService and the switcher, a missing forward-reference import, and the absence of a back-compat alias for the renamed public symbol. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — narrow the frame's ADT, document the handler contract, and add a deprecation alias before landing.
